cut: v2 full build (7 Nov, en only; approved by the owner 7 Nov ~00:50: "Approved, render it"). RFH, Roundup / glyphosate. The device: THE LABEL. One generic weedkiller jug on a shed workbench (no brand, no logo, no trade dress; Roundup is named in captions and tags only) is the stage, and each beat of the 2026 record happens to its label: a state cancer-warning sticker cannot stick (Durnell); a rubber stamp brands it a national-defense priority (the 18 Feb executive order); a NONNEGOTIABLE sticky note lands on a desk phone that never rings (Means's allegation, 6 Nov, attributed, with Kennedy's own March statement beside it); the warning box stays empty. v2 fixes: actions land on each caption's pop word; the claims are banker's boxes of files; the window is gone; caption 4 says 'consulted' (the sources' word). US spelling.
argument: In 2026 Roundup's fight moved onto its label: the Supreme Court preempted state cancer warnings, an order made glyphosate a defense priority, and an ex-adviser alleges Kennedy wasn't consulted; Bayer says it's safe.
syntax: '/' breaks a line, [word] is the pop word

captions.source: About 65,000 Roundup claims (Reuters via Insurance Journal, 3 Nov 2026; Bayer, Mar 2026): plaintiffs allege glyphosate caused their non-Hodgkin lymphoma. Bayer says Roundup is safe; the EPA (and EFSA) did not find glyphosate likely carcinogenic; IARC classified it 'probably carcinogenic to humans' in 2015. One verb for the allegation: 'allege'. Search summaries only.

text.en: Supreme Court: / no state cancer / [warning] on it.

captions.source: Monsanto Co. v. Durnell, No. 24-1068, decided 25 Jun 2026, 7–2 (Kavanaugh; Jackson and Gorsuch dissenting): FIFRA preempts a Missouri failure-to-warn claim that would have required a cancer warning on Roundup's label; a jury award of about $1.25M was reversed (Mayer Brown, Faegre Drinker, National Ag Law Center summaries). 'No state cancer warning on it' = a state-law claim cannot require one; the label is set under federal law (EPA). Search summaries only.

text.en: The White House / made it a / [defense] priority.

captions.source: Executive order of 18 Feb 2026, 'Promoting the National Defense by Ensuring an Adequate Supply of Elemental Phosphorus and Glyphosate-Based Herbicides', invoking the Defense Production Act (Washington Times, Fresh Fruit Portal, ADN, Feb 2026). MAHA activists objected; Kennedy backed it publicly and later told Rogan he was not 'particularly happy' with it (Feb 2026). Search summaries only.

text.en: An ex-adviser / alleges RFK Jr. / wasn't [consulted].

captions.source: Calley Means, former White House adviser (left 22 Oct 2026), on The Joe Rogan Experience #2578 (reported 6 Nov 2026: Axios, STAT, Yahoo News): he alleges Kennedy was not consulted when the White House backed the glyphosate makers at the Supreme Court or on the executive order, and that Wiles's deputies pushed the order as 'nonnegotiable'. Attributed allegation. Kennedy's own account, E&E News, 5 Mar 2026: 'I did know about the executive order, and I made my opinions about it clear to the administration' (shown on the tag beside it). HHS pointed Axios to a Kennedy post saying he and Trump would keep fighting. A rebuttal attributed to White House aide James Blair appears only in search summaries without a named outlet, so it is not used. 'Told RFK Jr. not to call the president' appears only in an advocacy group's clip (MAHA Action on X), so it is not used. Not used: Stephen Miller replacing Susie Wiles (6 Nov) — no link is claimed or shown. Search summaries only.

text.en: On the label: / still no / cancer [warning].

captions.source: The station's line, true as a description: Roundup's US label carries no cancer warning; after Durnell a state claim cannot require one. The EPA's position is that glyphosate is not likely carcinogenic. Bayer's $7.25B class settlement for current and future claims awaits final approval in St. Louis; Bayer's CEO said on 3 Nov he expects it before Christmas (Reuters via Insurance Journal); no ruling as of 7 Nov (search summaries: Claims Journal, Global Agriculture, Settlement Insight).

post.en: States can't require a cancer warning on Roundup, the Supreme Court ruled (7–2). A February order made glyphosate a defense priority. An ex-adviser alleges RFK Jr. wasn't consulted; Kennedy said in March he knew of it. Bayer says it's safe, as the EPA found. Who writes the label?
